definition.definition: Induction length = distance from shock to maximum positive thermicity; reaction width = spatial full width at half maximum of that connected positive thermicity peak. Use linear interpolation at half-maximum and report additional peaks separately.

case.physical_model: Single-phase inviscid reactive Euler, LiDryer, transverse uniform periodic strip; no droplets, diffusion or transverse perturbation.
case.initialization: Near-CJ finite-rate ZND at 1.00001 D_CJ; no forcing or imposed wave speed after initialization.

caveats: Global thermicity peak on the fixed 0–3 mm window. FWHM refers to its connected peak, not the full span of all pulses.
Peak position uses resolved sample maximum. Half-height crossings use linear interpolation. No smoothing.
The 4-us CFD fields are unsteady; these are instantaneous apparent lengths, not established steady ZND parameters.
Local shock speed is a derivative of output positions at about 0.25 us intervals, not a step-resolved velocity.
